worked_solution:
We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to -\infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{-2}\frac{4}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =4{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{\int }_{a}^{-2}{x}^{-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =4{lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[-{x}^{-1}]}_{a}^{-2} \\  & =-4\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }{[\frac{1}{x}]}_{a}^{-2} \\  & =-4\cdot {lim}_{a\to -\infty }[\frac{1}{(-2)}-\frac{1}{a}] \\  & =-4\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
